title: "Resources"
order: 2

External links for this lesson. All verified to load.

- **[eCFR homepage](https://www.ecfr.gov)** — the Electronic Code of Federal Regulations, the
  free, continuously updated, unofficial-but-authoritative online version of the CFR. This is
  where you look up any citation you're handed, and where the source text for this lesson came
  from.

- **[Understanding the eCFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/reader-aids/understanding-the-ecfr)** —
  eCFR's own explainer on how the CFR is structured (titles, chapters, parts, sections) and how
  the online edition relates to the official printed CFR published by the National Archives.
  Read this once if the title/chapter/subchapter/part/section breakdown in this lesson's
  decoder table needs reinforcing.

- **[21 CFR 606.160, current text](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-606/subpart-D/section-606.160)**
  — the live, continuously updated version of the exact section quoted in this lesson. Regulations
  get amended; this link always shows the current text, unlike the dated snapshot saved in this
  repo's `sources/` folder. Use this to check whether a section has changed since a lesson was
  written.

- **[GovInfo: Code of Federal Regulations](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/cfr)** — the
  U.S. Government Publishing Office's official, legally authoritative annual CFR archive (PDF
  and XML, by year). eCFR is the practical day-to-day tool; GovInfo is where you go if you ever
  need the official, dated, legally citable version of a specific year's CFR text — for
  example, to confirm exactly what a regulation said on the date of a past inspection.
